evidence: The portable sqlite-wal-v1 profile and runtime are byte-semantically equal and pin application ID ROBS, schema version 1, exact DDL fingerprint, WAL/FULL durability, foreign keys, defensive/trusted-schema/DQS/load-extension controls, busy timeout, checkpoint policy, and the canonical table inventory.

Fourteen STRICT tables separate stable aggregate identities from immutable revisions and normalized scholarly/document/workflow/evidence/ontology/decision projections. Only INTEGER, REAL, and TEXT are permitted; large derived content is represented by a SHA-256 object reference rather than arbitrary BLOB or payload columns.

Canonical IDs, project ownership, aggregate-kind relationships, true UTC millisecond timestamps, safe scalar ranges, append-only provenance, and single-project database identity are enforced by database constraints. A real WAL reader snapshot and competing writer smoke test passes.
Focused tests cover initialization, restart, project create/open integration, concurrent reader/writer and busy-writer behavior, typed inserts, and integrity reports.

Hostile tests deny wrong-project references, invalid UUIDs and timestamps, aggregate-kind mismatch, unsafe integers, non-finite reals, arbitrary binary settings, duplicate project identity, audit mutation, existing/hardlinked/mismatched database replacement, ATTACH, and forged sqlite_schema SQL.

ADR-0014 and the local SQLite architecture guide define the versioned schema, connection factory, transaction/migration boundaries, explicit integrity operations, T02/T03 ownership, and the still-deferred encryption boundary without claiming encryption is already implemented.

Project creation initializes and fully verifies the database before staging publication. Compatible open verifies immutable application/profile/schema fingerprint and project identity before lock or audit publication; full database-size integrity scans remain explicit for T02/T03 startup and maintenance scheduling.

Contracts, build schema inventory, quality scope, data test inventory, planning views, and review-site completion status are updated. No UI implementation, dependency, migration runner, repository layer, object encryption, secret management, or unrelated runtime behavior is introduced.
